title: Learned screening prioritizes FOS in human renal reperfusion data
summary: Researchers applied LASSO, random forest and support-vector-machine recursive feature elimination to renal transcriptomic data and converged on FOS and FOSB as candidates after kidney reperfusion. Both were elevated across 41 matched pre/post-reperfusion biopsy pairs, and an exploratory two-gene model reached an AUC of 0.922 on that discovery cohort; FOS alone performed similarly. In a separate dataset of 28 acute kidney injury biopsies and 11 stable controls, FOS remained elevated but FOSB did not. This is retrospective candidate evidence: the external dataset did not validate the combined diagnostic model, and the authors describe their analysis as exploratory rather than clinical model validation.
ai_technology: LASSO regression, random forest and support-vector-machine recursive feature elimination
organization: Renmin Hospital of Wuhan University; Wuhan University

evidence.tested: Three learned feature-selection approaches converged on FOS and FOSB in GSE126805, comprising 42 kidney-transplant recipients sampled at four time points; the paper excluded one unmatched post-reperfusion sample and analyzed 41 matched pre/post pairs. The exploratory two-gene ROC AUC of 0.922 and similar FOS-alone performance were estimated in this same discovery dataset, with no held-out evaluation reported. In the independent GSE30718 series (28 AKI biopsies and 11 stable controls), FOS remained elevated but FOSB did not. The authors explicitly characterize this as candidate-feature robustness assessment, not clinical validation of a diagnostic model.
evidence.unknown: The combined model was not independently evaluated; FOSB did not replicate in GSE30718, and FOS alone performed comparably in the discovery cohort. The study does not establish clinical utility, prospective performance, or a causal role for FOS/FOSB in lung-to-kidney signaling.
evidence.ai_role: LASSO, random forest and SVM-RFE feature selection identified FOS and FOSB from renal transcriptomic candidates; FOS was the more reproducible injury-associated candidate in the separate AKI cohort.

source_review.scope: Source-provenanced publisher JATS abstract, ML methods, paired-cohort analysis, results 3.3 and limitations; primary GEO metadata for GSE126805 and GSE30718. The represented claim is retrospective renal candidate evidence, not a validated diagnostic model or causal cross-organ mechanism.
